data.text:
Interesting from PewResearch 

After hitting a record 53.3 million in January (15.8% of the population), the foreign-born population fell to 51.9 million by June—the first decline since the 1960s. 

More are leaving or being deported than arriving.

Other highlights from the report:Immigrants make up ~19% of the U.S. workforce (down slightly in 2025).

In 2023: 
73% were legal (naturalized citizens, permanent residents, etc.); 
27% unauthorized (peaked at 14 million, a record high before recent drops).

Origins: 
Mexico still tops (~22%), followed by India, China, Philippines; Latin America ~52%, Asia ~27%.

Education: 
Immigrants match U.S.-born adults in bachelor's degrees or higher (36%), though lower high school completion for some groups.

English proficiency: 
52% speak it very well/only English at home, higher for longer-term arrivals.

Neutral, data-driven look at a shifting landscape. Full breakdown here: https://t.co/h4ClME9Rkz
What stands out to you in these numbers? #Immigration #USData #PewResearch

Sinuspinde ng Land Transportation Office (LTO) ang lisensya ng isang tuk-tuk driver sa loob ng 90 araw matapos masangkot sa banggaan at counterflow incident sa Pasay City na naglagay sa peligro sa mga motorista at pasahero.   

Naglabas din ang LTO ng Show Cause Order laban sa driver at rehistradong may-ari dahil sa mga paglabag tulad ng reckless driving at disregarding traffic signs, alinsunod sa direktiba ni Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. na panagutin ang mga abusadong motorista.
